policy_title: Urgent sentencing review with automatic life imprisonment for repeat violent offenders
stated: Reform UK will launch an urgent sentencing review, introducing mandatory life sentences for those committing second violent or serious offences.

source.quote: Urgent Sentencing Review with Automatic Life Imprisonment for Violent Repeat Offenders Those committing second violent or serious offences will receive mandatory life sentences.

bearing_set.reason: Mandatory life sentences for repeat violent offenders directly affects sentencing policy, deterrence, and justice system capacity — a core Safety & Security indicator.

Mandatory minimum/life sentencing removes judicial discretion over proportionality and mitigating circumstances, directly implicating due process — a named O9 indicator — via a concrete mechanism (courts bound regardless of case specifics).

Mandatory life sentences for all second serious-offence convictions would substantially expand the long-term prison population; each life sentence carries multi-decade costs (~£40k–50k/year in England and Wales), creating a concrete, sustained pressure on the funded-vs-borrowed and debt-path indicators under O12.

membership_note: Three fundamentals with distinct, mechanistically grounded bearings: the safety/protective effect (O5), the due-process/rule-of-law cost of removing judicial discretion (O9), and the long-run fiscal cost of mandatory life imprisonment at scale (O12).
